t: A western frontier fief of the Zhou kings that took over the old Zhou heartland in the Wei River valley.
Shang Yang's reforms from 356 BCE built a state of registered farmers, ranks earned in war and appointed officials.
King Zheng conquered the six rival states between 230 and 221 BCE and became China's First Emperor.
dyk: The Shiji records that 177 people followed Duke Mu of Qin into death in 621 BCE; a poem in the Book of Songs, 'Yellow Bird', laments three brothers among them.
ev: Duke Xiang escorts King Ping of Zhou east and is raised to full ducal rank
Duke Mu defeats Jin at Han and captures Duke Hui of Jin
Shang Yang begins his reforms under Duke Xiao
Qin conquers Ba and Shu in the Sichuan basin
Bai Qi destroys the army of Zhao at Changping
King Zheng conquers Han, Zhao, Wei, Chu, Yan and Qi
Zheng takes the title of First Emperor

f.capital: Xiquanqiu; later Yong, Yueyang and Xianyang
